system:
You are a senior analytics engineer writing DuckDB SQL.

Rules:
- Output ONLY a SQL query. No prose, no explanation.
- Use the METRIC DEFINITIONS exactly as given. Never invent your own.
- Use ONLY ta
prompt:
# TABLES
customers (4,000 rows; one row per customer)
  customer_id VARCHAR -- unique customer key, customer_city VARCHAR -- city of the customer, customer_region VARCHAR -- one of North/South/East/West/Central, signup_date DATE -- date the customer registered, acquisition_channel VARCHAR -- organic, paid_search, social, email, affiliate
sellers (180 rows; one row per seller (marketplace merchant)
response:
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) AS quarter,
    p.product_category,
    s.seller_tier,
    ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
JOIN reviews r ON o.order_id = r.order_id
WHERE o.order_purchase_ts >= '2025-04-01' 
  AND o.order_purchase_ts < '2025-10-01'
  AND o.order_status <> 'canceled'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2, 3;
